messages:
ivy: heads-up: premerge scan for PR #9023 shows SAST + DAST signals. artifact: gs://ci/9023/scan.json — looks like keystore.Decrypt used on a public endpoint.

ben: paste the snippets?

ivy:
```
SAST: config/handler.go:88 keystore.Decrypt(envKey) -> rule RDX-KMS-013
DAST: GET /public/status -> response includes 'cfg_part: <evaluated>' proof
```

rachel: tagging infra 14 any recent KMS rotations or RBAC grants for the public service?

oncall-sre: we rotated the staging key two days ago; no RBAC changes except a short-lived rollout grant for deployer-ci that should not include decrypt. I can repro and pull audit logs.

ben: I'll own the SAST triage. ivy can you open a ticket and attach the artifact + ask for keystore audit?

ivy: created RED-9987 and added the artifact link + triage checklist. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RED-9987

oncall-sre: repro notes: I replayed a grant in sandbox and saw GET /public/status include the evaluated fragment only when decrypt was present. Audit shows grant id G-8811 with decrypt inadvertently added.

rachel: found G-8811 in the keystore-change log and rolled it back. attaching audit slice to RED-9987. We'll add two-approver rule for any grant containing decrypt.

ben: quick code excerpt added to the ticket:
```
// handler.go
secret, _ := keystore.Decrypt(os.Getenv("CONFIG_KEY"))
w.Write([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("cfg_part: %s", secret)))
```
We should fail closed and never call Decrypt for public routes. Opening PR to require explicit key param and to redact output. PR: https://github.com/redwood/config/pull/1283 (WIP).

ivy: action items in RED-9987: ben -> code fix + test, rachel -> RBAC rollback + playbook update, oncall-sre -> attach audit export. ETA EOD.

security-bot: Reminder: ephemeral grants and keystore changes must reference the ticket and be recorded in the keystore-change log.

oncall-sre: export attached. ephemeral grant window closed.

ben: pushed sanitizer + test to PR, requesting review.

ivy: re-run premerge after PR merges and confirm scans are clean. Thanks team.

security-bot: Thread archived to RED-9987."
